objective_for_doctor:
Age: 2
Sex: M
Chief Complaint: jaw stiffness

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?
My jaw is stiff, and I suddenly have difficulty or an inability to open my mouth, with jaw pain when opening it.
When did the jaw stiffness and difficulty opening your mouth begin, and did it come on suddenly or develop gradually?
It came on suddenly.
Do you have any recent dental work, tooth pain, or a visible swelling or infection in your mouth or gums?
I don’t know.
Have you noticed any fever, chills, or feeling generally unwell since the jaw stiffness started?
I don't know.
Have you had any recent head or facial trauma, such as a blow to the jaw, or any recent surgeries or procedures in the head/neck area?
I don't know.
Are you experiencing any difficulty swallowing, drooling, or a sore throat that feels worse when you try to open your mouth?
I don't know.
Are you experiencing any pain, swelling, or tenderness in the area just in front of your ear (the temporomandibular joint) or around your jawbone, and is it on one side or both sides?
I don't know.
Do you take any medications regularly—especially antipsychotics, anti‑nausea drugs (like metoclopramide), muscle relaxants, or recent antibiotics?
I don’t know.
Do you recall when you last received a tetanus booster (Tdap or Td) vaccination?
I don’t know.
Do you have any recent or current sore throat, tonsillitis, or other upper‑respiratory infection symptoms (e.g., cough, runny nose, or recent skin wound)?
I don’t know.
Have you had any recent ear pain, ear infection, or a feeling of fullness in one ear?
I don’t know.

[ABSTAIN] Insufficient information – the patient’s responses provide only a sudden onset of trismus with jaw pain and no additional history, symptoms, or risk factors to reliably narrow the diagnosis.

[POSSIBLE] Tetanus, peritonsillar (quinsy) abscess, dental/odontogenic infection, temporomandibular joint disorder (acute TMJ dysfunction), medication‑induced dystonia (e.g., antipsychotic or anti‑nausea drug)
